identity.title: ALMA Observations of NGC 6334S. I. Forming Massive Stars and Clusters in Subsonic and Transonic Filamentary Clouds

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) and Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (JVLA) observations of the massive infrared dark cloud NGC 6334S

evidence.quote: The proximity of NGC 6334S (cite: 2014ApJ...784..114C) makes it an ideal laboratory to investigate the key physical processes related to massive star and cluster formation.
The uncertainty in distance from the trigonometric parallax measurement is about 20% (cite: 2014ApJ...784..114C).

question.value: Are non-thermal motions in the massive IRDC NGC 6334S subsonic/transonic at high resolution, and what is the dynamical state of its dense cores and velocity components?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we investigate the dynamical motions of identified embedded dense cores and their parent cloud, as well as the dynamical stability of dense cores.
using the 12-m main array of ALMA (ID: 2016.1.00951.S, PI: Shaye Strom)
Our 3 mm continuum image resolves 49 dense cores

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Two 234.4 MHz windows for H13CO+ 1-0 and NH2D 1_11-1_01 (61 kHz resolution); three 1.875 GHz continuum windows at 88.5, 98.5, 100.3 GHz

evidence.quote: We employed two 234.4 MHz wide spectral windows to cover the H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$ 1-0 (86.754 GHz) and NH$_{2}$D $1_{11}$-$1_{01}$ (85.926 GHz) lines, respectively
we centered three 1.875 GHz wide spectral windows at 88.5 GHz, 98.5 GHz, and 100.3 GHz to obtain broad band continuum data
We carried out a 55-pointings mosaic of the massive infrared dark cloud (IRDC), NGC 6334S
The projected baseline lengths range from 15 to 155 meters
This yields a synthesized beam of 3$^{\prime\prime}$.6 $\times$ 2$^{\prime\prime}$.4

analysis_steps.goal: identify dense cores in 3 mm continuum

method.value: astrodendro leaves, properties measured with CASA imfit; extra >5 sigma sources added

evidence.quote: We employed the `astrodendro`[^1] algorithm to pre-select dense cores (i.e., the leaves in the terminology of `astrodendro`) from the 3 mm continuum image
$\mathbf{min_{-}npix}$ = 40, which is approximately the synthesized beam area.

analysis_steps.goal: fit line profiles and velocity components

method.value: Pixel-by-pixel Gaussian fits to H13CO+ and NH2D (hyperfine) cubes; NH3 (1,1),(2,2) jointly fit for temperature

evidence.quote: We fit Gaussian line profiles to the H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$ image cube pixel by pixel, using the `PySpecKit` package

key_parameters.value: peaks >5 sigma separated by >2 channels are independent components; keep sigma_obs>3 err, -8<=vlsr<=0 km/s, I>3 err

evidence.quote: we regarded spectral peaks that are separated by more than 2 spectral channels and brighter than 5 times the rms noise level as independent velocity components

assumptions.value: Uniform T = 15 K where NH3 unavailable

evidence.quote: We use a uniform temperature of $\langle T_{\rm NH_{3}} \rangle$ = 15 K
We then simultaneously fit Gaussian profiles to all of the independent velocity components.

validation.value: Synthetic spectra smoothed to 0.21 km/s with noise, 1000 iterations, recovered input widths

evidence.quote: The fitted line width agrees with the input line width, indicating that the measured line widths are not significantly affected by the current spectral resolution in this study.

method.value: sigma_nt from sigma_obs minus channel and thermal terms; Mach = sqrt3 sigma_nt / c_s

evidence.quote: we also derived the Mach number, $\mathcal{M} = \sqrt{3} \sigma_{\rm nt}/c_{\rm s}$

assumptions.value: Mean gas mass 2.37 m_H; T from NH3 or 15 K

evidence.quote: assuming a mean mass of gas of 2.37$\, m_{\rm H}$ (cite: 2008A&A...487..993K)
found that 56% to up to 99% of Mach numbers are smaller than 2

method.value: Optically thin dust emission at 3 mm with Hildebrand opacity law; spherical density

evidence.quote: assuming optically thin modified black body emission in the Rayleigh-Jeans limit
where $\eta$ = 100 is the assumed gas-to-dust mass ratio
we estimate an uncertainty of 57% for the gas mass

method.value: Bertoldi & McKee virial mass with density power law and ellipsoidal geometry; component mass split by line intensity

evidence.quote: The virial ratio is evaluated for each decomposed structure using (cite: 1992ApJ...395..140B)
we assume a typical density profile of $b$ = 1.6 for all decomposed structures

assumptions.value: Prolate cores; intrinsic axis ratio from observed via Appell function

evidence.quote: the dense cores are likely prolate ellipsoids
the typical uncertainty is about 46% for the virial ratios

method.value: P_cl = pi G Sigma_bar Sigma_r beta_cl with SED column density; compare Omega_P, Omega_G, Omega_K

evidence.quote: $$P_{\rm cl} = \pi G \bar{\Sigma}\Sigma_{r}  \beta_{\rm cl},$$

key_parameters.value: Mean cloud column density 0.15 g/cm2; Sigma_r = Sigma_obs/2

findings_qualitative.value: Line widths increase with increasing beam size, suggesting poor resolution biases supersonic reports

evidence.quote: It is clear that the line widths increase with increasing beam sizes.

claims.hypothesis: Non-thermal motions in a massive IRDC are subsonic/transonic at ~0.02 pc
claims.experiment: Gaussian fits of H13CO+ and NH2D cubes, Mach numbers with NH3 temperatures
claims.result: ~77% of regions have M<=2; mean M 1.5
claims.finding: Motions are predominantly subsonic and transonic, like low-mass clouds

evidence.quote: the spatially unresolved non-thermal motions are predominantly subsonic and transonic ($\sim$77% regions)

claims.experiment: Virial analysis of 67 H13CO+ and 45 NH2D structures
claims.finding: More massive structures are more gravitationally unstable

evidence.quote: it is apparent that there is an inverse relationship between the mass and the virial ratio

claims.hypothesis: External pressure helps confine dense structures
claims.result: 79% bound with pressure vs 64% without; 14 remain unbound
claims.finding: External pressure plays a role in confinement

evidence.quote: This suggests that the external pressure plays a role in confining the dense structures in this early evolutionary stage of star formation region.

why_this_method.value: H13CO+ heavier than NH2D, better probe of non-thermal motions

evidence.quote: and therefore is a better probe of the non-thermal gas motions

limitations_admitted.value: Cannot discriminate causes of broad line widths in cores with the data at hand; filament pressure not computed

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, we can not discriminate between these possibilities with the data at hand.
We are not able to accurately compute the filament pressure

referee_caveats_inferred: Mass assigned to velocity components by line intensity fraction is crude
Fixed density slope and 15 K for much of the area
Spatially unresolved motions only partly addressed
Chemical segregation may bias virial masses
